title: Sign changes of Keiper-Li second differences
description: Let λn be the Keiper-Li coefficients and cn = λn+1 − 2λn + λn−1 their second differences, a sequence studied by Keiper in 1992, who showed that the Riemann hypothesis implies |cn| ≤ 2λ1. We study the sign of cn. We prove, without assuming the Riemann hypothesis, that cn is positive for infinitely many n and negative for infinitely many n. We also give a computer-assisted certificate, in exact interval arithmetic, that c1, ..., c117 > 0 and c118 < 0, which locates the first negative value; the value of c118 agrees with an independent public table. In particular, a conjecture of Xiao that cn > 0 for all n ≥ 2 first fails at n = 118 (Xiao's n = 119).
